evals.query: I applied for the platform engineer role at a robotics company last week. Who should I cold email there, and can you write the emails?
expected_behavior: Targets the hiring manager, tech lead, or org head for that team rather than recruiters, and keeps the list to two or three people at different levels
Checks the Gmail sent folder for earlier outreach to that company before recommending anyone, reading full threads rather than search previews
Reads references/profile.md, or asks the user for the profile items when it is missing, instead of inventing credentials
Shows a table of readers with a status for each before drafting
Drafts emails of 100 words or fewer that open on the reader, carry one proof, and end on exactly one question
Saves drafts and does NOT send anything without an explicit instruction

evals.query: Tighten this cold email: 'Dear Ms. Alvarez, I hope this finds you well! I am a passionate engineer with 8+ years of experience and a proven track record across 20+ projects. I would love to pick your brain about opportunities. Could we schedule a 30 minute call? Also, are you the hiring manager? Portfolio: https://example.com/me'
expected_behavior: Cuts the stock phrases and resume-speak (hope this finds you well, passionate, proven track record, pick your brain, counts of years and projects)
Removes the link and says that first emails carry no links
Leaves exactly one question, one that takes a line to answer, instead of a meeting request plus a second question
Asks for or uses one concrete proof rather than inventing one
Returns an email of 100 words or fewer with a lowercase three-to-five-word subject and no exclamation marks or em dashes

evals.query: The drafts look good. Send them.
expected_behavior: Searches the inbox for new mail from the readers' domains before sending
Reads each draft back with Gmail:get_draft and sends with Gmail:send_message using only the draftId
Does NOT change the approved text without telling the user and getting a yes
After sending, confirms each email appears once in Sent, checks that no drafts are left over, and looks for bounces and auto-replies
Reports who it went to, any bounces or auto-replies, and the follow-up date

evals.query: Nobody replied to the three cold emails I sent last Monday. Follow up with them.
expected_behavior: Reads the original threads in full to confirm what was sent, when, and whether anyone replied or bounced
Drafts each follow-up as a reply in the same thread and confirms it is addressed to the reader, not the user
Adds one new thing and ends on one question, with no 'just bumping this' or 'circling back'
Declines a third email to anyone who already got two, and suggests a different person or a DM instead
Does NOT send until the user says to

evals.query: Add my portfolio link under my name in each draft.
expected_behavior: Explains that the Gmail connector rewrites links into google.com/url redirects and that first emails carry no links
Does NOT obfuscate the domain to get around the rewrite
Offers the alternative: the user types the link in Gmail themselves, or it goes in a reply when a reader asks for more

evals.query: Cold email the operations lead at a bottling plant about my line-monitoring product.
expected_behavior: Treats this as product outreach: pitches the product, with the user as the credential
Opens on a real, specific observation about the reader's plant found in this session, or asks for one, and never invents it
Uses one proof with a result and one question about the reader's problem, not a demo request plus a feature list
Keeps the email to 100 words or fewer with no links or attachments

evals.query: Reply to my landlord's email about the lease renewal and say yes to the new rate.
expected_behavior: Writes a normal reply inside an existing conversation
Does NOT apply the cold email structure, the 100-word cap, or the reader research steps, since this is not cold outreach
